correctness.rationale: For the stipulated scalar ODE, f=(1-x)P-1 has degree M and f(1)=-1. Local asymptotic stability at an interior zero requires a positive drift just left and a negative drift just right, even when the zero is not hyperbolic, since a nonzero polynomial has isolated zeros. Each pair of consecutive attractors therefore costs an intervening zero; 2k-1<=M gives the claimed bound. In the proposed construction the coefficient sum bound follows from the product of one plus each small positive root of Q. The geometric-series baseline gives exactly -x^M; at each of the M interleaved test points all factor distances are at least delta/(2M), so the perturbation dominates by at least 4(1-delta)>1. The alternating signs and the negative right boundary yield M distinct interior roots of a degree-M polynomial, necessarily simple. Working leftwards from the right boundary gives exactly ceil(M/2) attractors, and the strict signs persist on an open positive-coefficient neighborhood. The sign at x=0 has the stated even/odd orientation. Inspected RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and verify.py. The rational sign certificates for M=2 through 12 are supplementary and were not rerun. This verifies the scalar theorem only, not an all-order rigorous stochastic-to-mean-field limit; the cited source treats the latter as conjectural.
